newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK fourth quarter 1996 revised GDP.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK fourth quarter 1996 revised GDP.

text.p: Following is a series of reactions to UK fourth quarter 1996 revised gross domestic product data published at 0930 GMT. The figures showed Q4 GDP of 2.7 percent year-on-year and 0.8 percent quarter-on-quarter.
"We've seen a nudge up in the headline and underlying measures. Further robust growth coming through on the consumer spending side."
"The data are not wholly surprising, but they are showing a continued robust picture of consumer spending which will fuel worries about further growth this year."
"The figures confirm the economy was growing above trend at the end of last year. The breakdown clearly shows that the bulk of growth is on the consumer side."
"The inflation component still remains pretty healthy, but overall the data will not have any impact on the current policy debate."

KEVIN GARDINER, MORGAN STANLEY "The data don't the initial impression significantly. They confirm that the economy was growing comfortably at an above trend rate and would have grown even more rapidly if it hadn't been for a sharp fall in agricultural output."

"Looking to the new year, I see very few signs of this growth rate slowing down. If anything, I think we might have accelerated slightly. So, as to what this tells us about interest rates, I think the Bank of England is on the right track."
"The data are very much in line with the provisional numbers. They continue the story of a very strong UK economy, led by a very sharp increase in consumer spending."
